# MCP Masterclass 🎓

The definitive guide to building production-ready AI agents with the Model Context Protocol.


The **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** is an open standard that allows AI models to securely connect to external tools and datasets. This repository takes you from high-level architecture down to production-grade deployment, teaching you how to build robust, secure, and scalable MCP servers using Python and the `FastMCP` SDK. --- ## 📑 Table of Contents - [Why This Masterclass?](#-why-this-masterclass) - [The Anatomy of an AI Agent](#-the-anatomy-of-an-ai-agent) - [Prerequisites & Quick Start](#-prerequisites--quick-start) - [Curriculum Syllabus](#-curriculum-syllabus) - [Theory: Chapters](#-theory-chapters) - [Practice: Labs](#-practice-labs) - [Mastery: Capstone Projects](#-mastery-capstone-projects) - [Recommended Ecosystem Tools](#-recommended-ecosystem-tools) - [Contributing](#-contributing) - [License](#-license) --- ## 🌟 Why This Masterclass? - 🚀 **Zero to Production**: Learn everything from basic protocol handshakes to advanced zero-trust security and multi-server orchestration. - 🛠️ **FastMCP Native**: Built entirely on the modern, asynchronous Python SDK (`FastMCP`). No boilerplate, just business logic. - 🛡️ **Enterprise Ready**: Deep dives into Human-in-the-Loop workflows, robust error handling, and secure binary data streaming. - 🎓 **Hands-On Capstones**: Don't just read—build! Construct real-world agents like Clinical Copilots and Autonomous Dev Assistants. --- ## 🧠 The Anatomy of an AI Agent Before building MCP servers, it's crucial to understand where MCP fits into the broader AI ecosystem. There are three primary **Participants**: 1. **MCP Host**: The AI application (like Claude Desktop, Cursor, or your custom app) that orchestrates the entire experience. 2. **MCP Client**: A component inside the Host that maintains the connection to servers and negotiates capabilities. 3. **MCP Server**: The service (what you will build) that provides tools, resources, and context to the Client. As shown below, a production-grade AI Agent is a complex, multi-layered architecture:
> **The MCP Layer** acts as the strict, standardized protocol boundary between the Agent Orchestration layer and your bottom-tier external tools. It ensures all tool routing, data fetching, and validation is secure and standardized. --- ## 💻 Prerequisites & Quick Start If you are only reading the theoretical **Chapters**, no installation is required! However, to participate in the hands-on **Labs** and **Projects**, you will need: - **Python 3.13+** installed on your system. - An **API Key** from an LLM provider (e.g., Anthropic, OpenAI) for testing live agents. - **Node.js** installed (required to run the MCP Inspector). ### Quick Start ```bash # 1. Install the core SDK pip install mcp # 2. Navigate to the first lab cd labs/lab-01-hello-mcp # 3. Run your server using the official Inspector UI npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector python server.py ``` --- ## 📚 Curriculum Syllabus This masterclass is designed to be highly practical. We recommend the "Read, Build, Master" approach: read a chapter, execute the corresponding lab, and finish with the capstone projects. ### 📖 Theory: Chapters *Learn the mental models and architectural patterns.* - 📍 **Level 1: Foundations** - [Chapter 1: The Big Picture](chapters/01-the-big-picture/README.md) - [Chapter 2: Environment Setup](chapters/02-environment-setup/README.md) - [Chapter 3: The Handshake](chapters/03-the-handshake/README.md) - 🏗️ **Level 2: Builder** - [Chapter 4: Tool Definition](chapters/04-tool-definition/README.md) - [Chapter 5: Resource Management](chapters/05-resource-management/README.md) - [Chapter 6: The Transport Layer](chapters/06-the-transport-layer/README.md) - 🏛️ **Level 3: Architect** - [Chapter 7: Security & Auth](chapters/07-security-and-auth/README.md) - [Chapter 8: Prompts & Templates](chapters/08-prompts-and-templates/README.md) - [Chapter 9: Real-World Integration](chapters/09-real-world-integration/README.md) - [Chapter 10: Deployment & Scale](chapters/10-deployment-and-scale/README.md) - [Chapter 11: Client & Orchestration](chapters/11-client-and-orchestration/README.md) - [Chapter 12: Advanced Architecture](chapters/12-advanced-mastery/README.md) ### 🔬 Practice: Labs *Build and test the core primitives locally.* - 🧪 [Lab 1: Run MCP locally](labs/lab-01-hello-mcp/README.md) - 🧪 [Lab 2: Build a tool server](labs/lab-02-tool-server/README.md) - 🧪 [Lab 3: Add resource context](labs/lab-03-resource-server/README.md) - 🧪 [Lab 4: Prompts & Templates](labs/lab-04-prompts-and-templates/README.md) - 🧪 [Lab 5: Add security layer](labs/lab-05-secure-tools/README.md) - 🧪 [Lab 6: Multi-server orchestration](labs/lab-06-multi-server-agent/README.md) ### 🏆 Mastery: Capstone Projects *See how enterprise micro-servers orchestrate together to solve complex domain problems.* - 💻 **[AI Dev Assistant](projects/ai-dev-assistant/README.md)** - Expose Git and linters; build an agent that fixes its own bugs. - 🏥 **[Clinical Copilot](projects/clinical-copilot/README.md)** - Implement zero-trust PII scrubbing and Human-in-the-Loop workflows for healthcare data. - 📊 **[Data Agent](projects/data-agent/README.md)** - Turn an LLM into a SQL analyst by streaming database schemas via Resources. - 🗺️ **[Maps Grounding Agent](projects/maps-grounding-agent/README.md)** - Ground your AI in reality using the official Google Maps MCP server. --- ## 🤝 Recommended Ecosystem Tools To get the most out of MCP, we highly recommend integrating with these powerful frameworks: - **[LangChain](https://www.langchain.com/)**: The industry standard framework for building context-aware reasoning applications. Perfect for acting as the Orchestrator/Client for your MCP servers. - **[Agent Development Kit (ADK)](https://adk.dev/)**: An essential toolkit for rapidly developing, testing, and deploying intelligent agents that consume MCP tools. --- ## 🛠️ Contributing We welcome contributions! If you have ideas for new labs, improvements to existing chapters, or bug fixes: 1. Fork the repository. 2. Create your feature branch (`git checkout -b feature/AmazingFeature`). 3. Commit your changes (`git commit -m 'Add some AmazingFeature'`). 4. Push to the branch (`git push origin feature/AmazingFeature`). 5. Open a Pull Request. --- ## 📄 License Distributed under the MIT License. See `LICENSE` for more information. ---
